text: Which team will win the 2026 FIFA World Cup?

Squad continuity between winning World Cup tournaments has not reliably produced back-to-back titles for national teams in the tournament's history.
Teams with a reigning Golden Boot winner from the previous World Cup have historically had above-average odds of winning the next tournament.
Individual player awards from a prior World Cup do not determine which national team wins the subsequent tournament.
Player performance in elite international football typically declines with age, especially for players over 35.
Squad age averages correlate only weakly with FIFA World Cup outcomes historically, since tournament success depends heavily on tactics, form, and squad depth rather than average age alone.

Historical patterns of which national teams win World Cups held on a given continent tend to persist across tournaments due to shared factors like travel fatigue, climate adaptation, and fan support that favor teams from the host continent.
The number of prior FIFA World Cup tournaments held outside Europe is too small to establish a reliable historical base rate for any single team's performance in host-region conditions.
A larger tournament field statistically dilutes the probability that any single favored team, such as Spain, France, England or Argentina, wins.
